_readme: DRAFT seed list. Distances/gain are ranges because sources disagree by route variant (AllTrails, Modern Hiker, HikeSpeak, Hike Los Angeles, LA County Parks, 2026-10-07 web search). Descriptions are placeholders written from those guides, not first-hand: rewrite in your own voice. No coordinates yet; add from OSM later. status: open | closed | verify.

trails.name: Runyon Canyon Loop
trails.trailhead: Runyon Canyon Park, Hollywood (Fuller Ave / Vista St entrances)
trails.description: Busy urban loop with steady climbs and wide views of Hollywood and downtown. Good for a quick sweat with friends and a sunset finish. Little shade. Hero Trail variant is steeper (about 1,000 ft).

trails.name: Eagle Rock Canyon Trail
trails.trailhead: Eagle Rock View Dr / Richard Alatorre Park, Eagle Rock
trails.description: Short neighborhood loop maintained by the community, with seven switchbacks up the south side and views of the Verdugo Hills and downtown. A 30-minute after-work hike.
trails.status_source: user confirmed this is the intended trail; open status unverified

trails.name: Solstice Canyon (Malibu)
trails.trailhead: Solstice Canyon Park, Corral Canyon Rd, Malibu
trails.route_type: out-and-back (or loop with Rising Sun Trail)
trails.description: Gentle canyon walk to a small waterfall and the ruins of a burned house. The Rising Sun Trail loop adds a steep climb and ocean views. Good first Malibu hike. Check Santa Monica Mountains park status after the 2025 fires.

trails.name: Escondido Falls (Malibu)
trails.description: Residential road walk, then a creek-side trail to a roughly 50 ft lower waterfall. The upper tier needs a steep unmaintained scramble across private land and has had access restrictions.

trails.name: Culver City Stairs (Baldwin Hills Scenic Overlook)
trails.trailhead: Hetzler Rd & Jefferson Blvd, Culver City
trails.description: About 282 steep steps straight up roughly 300 ft, then a switchback trail down. Panoramic view across LA from the Baldwin Hills overlook. A burner workout in under an hour.

trails.name: Eaton Canyon Falls (Nature Center trailhead)
trails.trailhead: Eaton Canyon Nature Center, 1750 N Altadena Dr, Pasadena
trails.status_note: LA County: Eaton Canyon Natural Area and trails closed through at least 2027-12-31 after the Eaton Fire; fines up to $5,000. Keep in the data for when it reopens.
trails.description: Flat wash for the first mile, then a narrow rocky canyon with many creek crossings to a roughly 40 ft waterfall. Wet feet likely.

trails.name: Eaton Canyon Falls (Pinecrest / Mt Wilson gate)
trails.status_note: Part of the Eaton Canyon closure (Angeles National Forest side). Verify with ANF before any visit.
trails.description: The short way to Eaton Falls: about 0.8 mi each way from the upper entrance, downhill on the way in so the climb is on the way out.

trails.name: Millard Canyon Falls
trails.description: Short creek-side walk past the trail camp to a roughly 50 ft waterfall that often runs dry and flows best after storms. Several stream crossings. Currently closed by the Eaton Fire area closure order.
trails.status_source: AllTrails, Time Out and Angeles National Forest closure notices (web search 2026-10-07)
trails.status_note: Covered by the Angeles National Forest Eaton Fire area closure order through 2027-12-31 (campground fire damage; Chaney Trail road access closed). Verify with the Angeles National Forest before any visit.

trails.name: Gabrielino Trail from JPL to Brown Mountain Dam
trails.trailhead: Lot near JPL / Windsor Ave, Altadena (top of Hahamongna Watershed Park)
trails.description: Starts paved behind JPL, turns to dirt, and follows the Arroyo Seco with a lot of shade to Brown Mountain debris dam. Mostly flat, so long but easy on the legs.

trails.name: Hahamongna Watershed Loop
trails.trailhead: Hahamongna Watershed Park, Oak Grove Dr, Pasadena
trails.description: Easy, mostly flat loop in the basin below JPL; the first half mile shares the Gabrielino Trail. A good low-effort option, not far from where you'd start the Brown Mountain Dam hike.

trails.name: Griffith Park: Fern Dell to Mount Hollywood
trails.trailhead: Fern Dell Dr & Black Oak Dr, Los Feliz
trails.description: Shaded stream walk through Fern Dell, then up past Griffith Observatory to the Mount Hollywood summit with views of the Hollywood sign and the basin. The classic big Griffith day.

trails.name: Griffith Park: Fern Dell to Griffith Observatory
trails.trailhead: Fern Dell Dr & Black Oak Dr, Los Feliz
trails.description: Shorter version of the Fern Dell climb that ends at the observatory terrace. Good for visitors who want the view without the summit.

trails.name: Griffith Park: Vista View Point (helipad) and Cedar Grove loop
trails.trailhead: Top of N Commonwealth Ave / Commonwealth Canyon Dr, Los Feliz (free street parking)
trails.description: Loop on the Los Feliz side of Griffith Park, about 2.3 miles with roughly 400 ft of elevation change and mostly paved road. Go up Commonwealth Canyon Drive, turn right on Vista Del Valle Drive, loop the Cedar Grove, then continue to Vista View Point (the helipad) for panoramic views of the city and the Hollywood sign. It is quieter than the Fern Dell and observatory routes. Vista Del Valle Drive also connects to Mount Hollywood Drive for a longer loop.
trails.status_note: Trailhead and elevation from HikeSpeak; confirm the start that matches your usual parking spot.

trails.name: Deukmejian Wilderness Park: Dunsmore Canyon and Le Mesnager Loop
trails.description: Climb up Dunsmore Canyon beside the stream, then return on the steeper Le Mesnager Loop with lookouts over the foothills and Verdugos. Parking gate has historically opened at 7 a.m. with street parking available.

trails.name: Mount Lukens via Dunsmore Canyon
trails.description: Long, hard climb from Deukmejian to the summit of Mount Lukens. Suggested extra for when the shorter loop gets easy. gain_ft unknown from sources; verify and check ANF closures.

trails.name: La Tuna Canyon Trail
trails.trailhead: La Tuna Canyon Rd, Sun Valley
trails.description: Steady climb through La Tuna Canyon Park to the Verdugo Motorway. Mostly exposed, so go early or on a cool day. The 2017 La Tuna fire closed it for a while, so verify current status.

trails.name: Verdugo Peak via Hostetter Fire Road
trails.trailhead: La Tuna Canyon Rd, Sun Valley
trails.description: Fire-road grind to Verdugo Peak (3,126 ft), the high point of the Verdugo Mountains. No shade; bring plenty of water.

trails.name: Mugu Peak (Point Mugu State Park)
trails.description: Steep, sun-exposed climb to a coastal peak with big ocean views, with shorter loop options. A bigger Malibu day than Solstice.
